summary: You wrote a competent, well-structured ethics report: your for/against discussion is balanced, your NHS and VW case studies ground the argument, and your four-point recommendation for Rachel is justified. To reach the top band, deepen stakeholder analysis (especially the chip contractor), strengthen and complete your references, add visual elements, and proofread carefully — several language errors currently hold your structure/language mark back.
next_steps: Add at least one figure or table (e.g. a stakeholder–impact matrix or decision flowchart) to support the discussion, as the rubric's top level requires several visual element types used competently.

Develop the 'chip contract company' stakeholder you introduce but never analyse, and extend decision-making conclusions to other stakeholders (health department, clients), not just Rachel and her company.

Fix the reference list: add the missing URL for reference [3], replace or better integrate the loosely relevant CNBC/Apple source, and correct the 'EACE' abbreviation to the full Engineers Australia Code of Ethics.
Rewrite the circular recommendation item 3 ('switch to a longer product cycle until they have the resources to achieve a six-month product cycle') so the proposed action is logically coherent.

Proofread thoroughly: correct 'DICUSSION', 'The economic benefits of could', 'have her company might go under', and 'ofprofessional', and state your word count to confirm you are within the 1,500-word limit.

criteria.C1: Very good (8/10). You identify several ethical issues — public safety, professional integrity, trust, business survival — and link them to engineering design, addressing both organisational context and stakeholders. To reach Excellent, describe the issues in more depth in the introduction and follow through on every stakeholder you list: the chip contract company is named but never analysed.
criteria.C2: Very good (8/10). Your objective for/against arguments (competitive advantage, revenue, harm, integrity, reputation) have reasonable depth, and you draw conclusions. For Excellent, extend decision-making recommendations beyond Rachel and her company to other stakeholders such as the health department and clients, with guidance on how each should decide.
criteria.C3: Very good (8/10). The body follows a logical for/against structure with linked paragraphs, and your conclusion is supported by the arguments and case studies. To reach Excellent, make every link compelling — the competitor counterfactual currently reads as speculative — and demonstrate a fully systematic understanding of the issues for all stakeholders.
criteria.C4: Very good (8/10). Four references including two external case studies (NHS, VW) provide both qualitative and quantitative evidence, such as lost letters and fines. For Excellent, broaden the reference base, ensure each source directly substantiates its claim (the CNBC/Apple article is only loosely relevant), and complete reference [3] with its URL.
criteria.C5: Good (6/10). All required sections are present with an appropriate abstract and IEEE-style references, but no figures, tables or visual elements are used, and there are several language errors ('DICUSSION', 'The economic benefits of could', 'have her company might go under', 'ofprofessional'). Fixing these and adding visuals would lift you to Very good or Excellent.
